summary: Steel fire tower on Bear Mountain's summit, dated 1923 by the register, removed around 1930; the stone Perkins tower beside it still stands.

facts.design: steel frame tower with nine landings and an observation cab
facts.status_note: Steel tower removed; the stone Perkins Memorial Tower about 300 ft away still stands. The register reports footings on the summit rock.

access.note: Summit lies within Harriman/Bear Mountain State Park. Only footings are reported at the steel tower site.

visit.trail_note: The Appalachian Trail passes the base of the stone Perkins Memorial Tower, which the register says is open to the public.

events.note: Steel fire tower erected on the summit by the State Park Commission, with the State Conservation Department; 60 feet, nine landings
1929 newspaper describes a steel fire observation tower recently raising the summit eighty feet; conflicts with the 1923 date
Register main text says removed in 1930, hedged as 'it's said'; its epilog gives 1930 unhedged; a 1932 survey still describes the tower, and a 2005 note says gone before 1965

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The steel tower is gone; the stone Perkins Memorial Tower on the same summit, about 300 feet to the west, still stands and is a separate record.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved dates: erection 1923 (register) versus a 1929 newspaper describing a steel tower recently raising the summit; removal 1930 (register, hedged 'it's said'), versus a 1932 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description that still describes the steel tower, versus a 2005 geocaching note giving removal before 1965. Height: 60 ft (register) versus about 65 ft (1932 survey). The register's footings observation is undated. Separate record: the stone Perkins Memorial Tower (us-ny-perkins-memorial) is standing and is not covered here. The FFLA list gives this tower's point as 41.31283, -74.00613, about 160 m from the Perkins point (41.31150, -74.00685); the steel tower's own point was not checked.
